newsitem.title: CANADA: Westcoast sees gas plant at full tilt Sat.
newsitem.headline: Westcoast sees gas plant at full tilt Sat.

text.p: Wescoast Energy Inc expects its problem-plagued McMahon natural gas processing plant in northeast British Columbia to be back at full capacity on Saturday, a company spokeswoman said on Friday.

"I understand that they've left the force majeure in effect because we're still trying to determine the exact nature of the problem, so there's a lot of testing going on," Westcoast's Patricia Bowles said in a phone interview from Vancouver.
"But as of tomorrow, all constraints will be lifted."
Processing at the 650 million cubic feet per day plant was cut back to 76 to 77 percent of capacity on Thursday when week-long problems with its sulphur unit intensified.
The facility was shut down for a few hours on Tuesday and declared -- then quickly lifted -- a force majeure on Wednesday owing to the sulphur train problems.
McMahon, built 30 years ago, is Westcoast's largest processing plant and a major collection center for northeast B.C.'s gas production.
Over the past year, it has suffered several outages leading to discontent among B.C. gas producers and marketers over its reliability.
Bowles said the company was planning to take mount a major review of the operational systems at McMahon, which is located near the town of Fort St. John.
"We are determined to stop these things from happening and there will be a very deep look at the plant and some of the issues around it." she said.
